messages:
Priya: Morning — consolidated the monthly recurring-incident signals into one heatmap. Pulled severity, tenant-impact, and root-cause buckets for Jan-Mar. Sharing summary and asking for owners to claim fixes. Link: https://redwood.docs/ops/incident-heatmap-mar2026

Diego: skimmed the heatmap. Looks like the top signal is "config drift during canary" (high frequency, medium impact). I can take lead on audit tooling to detect drift.

Sam: I can collaborate with Diego. We should add a pre-deploy validator that checks rollout config vs router policy. Quick win: lint rule + CI check.

Priya: adding action: "Config drift detection & preflight checks" | Owner: Diego | Collaborator: Sam | Due: 2026-03-28 | Notes: lint + CI gate + dashboard alert.

Nina: another cluster is "cache coherence after scaling" — different from KV invalidation; this is multi-tenant cache tombstoning after pod restarts. I propose a short postmortem specifically for that.

Maya: agree. Nina, can you scope the PM so we can triage contributing factors (migration, restart order, GC)?

Nina: will draft. Target: investigation doc by 2026-03-19.

Priya: noted. Action: "Cache coherence postmortem" | Owner: Nina | Due: 2026-03-19. Marking severity=high for tenants affected.

Diego: there's also a recurring signal for "silent retry storms" when upstream auth fails and our clients retry with no backoff. That's causing amplification and hitting third-party quotas.

Sam: short-term fix: global token bucket on outbound auth calls + exponential backoff with jitter. Long-term: local token caching + circuit breaker.

Priya: action: "Outbound auth throttling (temp + long-term)" | Owner: Sam | Due: 2026-04-08 | Notes: implement token bucket + cb.

Maya: ops question: how are we prioritizing these? Some are frequent but low-customer-impact. We should add a weighted score (freq x impact) and schedule based on that.

Priya: yes — heatmap already includes severity weight. I'll upload a ranked list and create a 6-week remediation cadence.

Diego: on tooling: I volunteer to add a nightly signal aggregator job that posts a short digest to #incidents with the top 3 trending signals. Could reduce surprise spikes.

Maya: that would help SRE. Also recommend we add a runbook gap column in the tracker: Y/N and link to missing steps. Too many fixes stall because runbooks are incomplete.

Priya: good point. Action: "Add runbook completeness field + link" | Owner: Priya | Due: 2026-03-17.

Nina: question for product: are customer-facing incidents being surfaced to success teams? We need better comms on tenants impacted by recurring patterns.

Sam: product comms is separate but we can add an incident tag in the tracker for "requires-customer-notify". That will ping CS on assignment.

Priya: done. Implemented tag in tracker and updated process doc.

SRE Bot: Reminder: add items to /incident-tracker using format: "Title | Owner | Due | Notes".

Priya: summary of owners/dates: Diego (config drift tooling) 2026-03-28, Nina (cache coherence PM & postmortem) 2026-03-19, Sam (auth throttling) 2026-04-08, Priya (runbook field) 2026-03-17. Will schedule a 30-min sync to align owners and unblock infra dependencies. Invite: 2026-03-18 09:30 PT.

Maya: propose rotating remediation lead every 4 weeks so no single owner holds too many action items. Volunteers: Diego -> Nina -> Sam in that order?

Diego: fine with that rotation.

Nina: ok.

Sam: yep.

Priya: final note: we'll track progress on the heatmap board and revisit in the April ops review. Please update status in the tracker before the sync.

Maya: thanks everyone. Closing thread; will follow up in the calendar invite.

SRE Bot: Reminder scheduled: "Monthly incident-signal checkin" on 2026-04-15 09:00.
